title: Chicago Blackhawks game tonight vs. Toronto Maple Leafs at United Center marks centennial celebration for NHL team
text:

 Chicago Blackhawks celebrating 100 years as a franchise during game against Toronto Maple Leafs 
 Over the last century, they have won 6 Stanley Cups. 
 The Blackhawks are celebrating 100 years as a franchise. WLS By Jasmine Minor , Poinesha Barnes Tuesday, November 17, 2026 11:33PM Share Follow ABC7 on Google CHICAGO (WLS) -- The Blackhawks are celebrating 100 years as a franchise. Their very first season started 100 years ago Tuesday, with a 4-1 win over Toronto.
 On Tuesday night, the Hawks close out their centennial celebration against that same franchise, now the Toronto Maple Leafs.
 ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch 
 The team has become a crucial part of Chicago's identity.
 Over the last century, they have won six Stanley Cups and a place among hockey royalty: the "Original Six."
 "It's fairly overwhelming, just in thinking about, you know, how much happened in the world in 100 years," Danny Wirtz said.
 But the kingdom bought by the Wirtz family in 1954 has made it through the century.
 "The things that we originated, whether it's the anthem, the goal horn, the butterfly goaltending," Danny Wirtz said.
 The kings of the game called it home, Bobby Hull and Stan Mikita, who delivered the 1961 cup. Then came the great Tony Esposito.
 "That mask, and it was so iconic. And that was one of the first images that I actually recall as a youngster," Danny Wirtz said.
 At the time, Danny Wirtz's grandfather, Bill Wirtz, kept regular-season home games off local TV, believing it would take away from the home crowd. For most fans, the only way to see a home game was from the seats of the madhouse on Madison.
 "It was loud. It was smoky. It was rough around the edges, and it was a magical place to grow up," Danny Wirtz said.
 But the games that were on TV were setting the stage for the next star to cross the border.
 "Every Saturday night, our family rule was we watch hockey, and of course the Hawks played the Canadiens many times," Denis Savard said.
 "I feel like it was meant to happen," Savard said.

 In 1980, the Hawks drafted Savard third overall, and he made the "spin-o-rama" his trademark.
 "I didn't do it for fans, but it worked," Savard said.
 By 2004, the kingdom took a hard dip. ESPN ranked the Hawks the worst franchise in all of professional sports. That was until the Hawks took hockey outdoors at Wrigley Field.
 "It was cold, but it also was like one of those early indicators that the Blackhawks were absolutely back in the consciousness of the Chicago and national fan base," Danny Wirtz said.
 That spring, Forbes called the Hawks' comeback the greatest sports-business turnaround ever.
 In 2010, the Hawks ended a 49-year Cup drought: then came 2013 and 2015 on home ice.
 They won three Cups in six seasons.
 The same ESPN that ranked them last later put that run among the 10 greatest dynasties in NHL history. Six cups in all: Only three teams have more.
 Danny Wirtz's father, Rocky, died in 2023.
 Now, as the Hawks turn 100, Danny Wirtz is leading a rebuild and trying to open the game to new fans.
 "There can be an insular component to the sport of hockey. So we're trying to find new entry points for kids to come into the sport," Danny Wirtz said.
 That means putting sticks in kids' hands through the park district and boys and girls clubs, and the $7 billion 1901 Project around the United Center, which ownership calls the largest private investment ever on the West Side.
 A century in, Chicago is still handing this team down: one generation to the next.
 Limited-edition centennial programs are available for the first 8,000 fans through the doors Tuesday.
 Chris Chelios, Jeremy Roenick, Eddie Olczyk and Pat Foley will be in attendance. It's the first time all five Hawks ambassadors have appeared together.
 Puck drop against is at 6:30 p.m.
